text.en: Asha moved a magnet near a coil connected to a small bulb and the bulb glowed for a moment. "Magnetism made electricity!" she cried.

The region around a magnet where its influence is felt is the magnetic field. A magnetic field line is a curve whose tangent at any point gives the direction of the field, and magnetic flux is the number of field lines passing through an area. A current-carrying wire also produces a magnetic field around it, which is the magnetic effect of current.
A conductor carrying current in a magnetic field feels a force, and its direction is given by Fleming's left hand rule. This force is used in the electric motor, which changes electrical energy into mechanical energy.
When the magnetic flux linked with a closed coil changes, an emf is induced. This is electromagnetic induction, and Lenz's law says the induced current flows so as to oppose the change that causes it. The electric generator uses it to change mechanical energy into electrical energy.
A transformer changes alternating voltage. A step-up transformer changes a low voltage to a high voltage and a step-down transformer changes a high voltage to a low voltage. Transformers work only with alternating current.

problem.en: A transformer has 100 primary turns and 500 secondary turns. Is it step-up or step-down?

text.en: Compare the turns of the two coils.
The secondary has more turns than the primary.
So it is a step-up transformer.

prompt.en: A friend says A magnet and a coil must always be moving apart to give current. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Any change in magnetic flux through the coil induces an emf.
Moving towards or away both work.

points.en: A motor turns electrical energy into motion.
Transformers step voltage up or down.
